source_observations.observation: Colophon identifies the compiler and first edition dated 2006.
Gujarati labels the section ઈચ્છાદર્શક પ્ર.પુ.એ.વ.; neighboring active -āmi cells independently disambiguate first-person singular.
The left-hand root and voice column places vṛdh and vṛt in middle rows.
The paired words in PG405 can now be assigned to the person–number declared in the contents.
An active kṛp row precedes two middle kṛp rows. Their first present forms distinguish the short and expanded primary. Gup begins the next root.
The middle rows separately print the short-primary and expanded-primary words ending in ñcakre. The active row immediately above has the active auxiliary.

source_observations.locator: Haima Dhātuparāyaṇa, entry 955 continuing on the following leaf
source_observations.observation: The lexicon entry for vṛt is distinct from row numbering in the modern handbook.
Syand and vṛdh have their own entries. The lexicon supplies desiderative stem evidence as a different level from a whole perfect word.
Śṛdh has the śabdakutsā gloss and kṛp the capacity gloss. The kṛp discussion distinguishes the setting with a middle and the setting outside it.
Auxiliary voice can refer to the root from which ām is formed.
The perfect formation and auxiliary inventory give the construction for reading the printed kṛ words.
The au-marked group has an optional i in the stated middle environment.
Kṛp has a separate prohibition outside the middle environment.
